operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case (Artist_ID, Famous_Release_date, Music_Festival); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
DDL mixes quoting styles: CREATE TABLE uses "..." but FK clauses use backticks (`Artist_ID` REFERENCES `artist`).
All columns are declared NOT NULL=0 (nullable) and no CHECK/UNIQUE constraints; only PKs and 2 FKs.
Date-like columns are declared TEXT (Famous_Release_date, Issue_Date, Date_of_ceremony) -> dispatch to String fuzzer, not Date.
Date text formats are heterogeneous and non-ISO: 'November 2007', 'January 21, 2008', '2009', '27 December 1986 - 10 January', '17 January', '9 May', '18 February 2011'.
Volume_Issue values are issue codes like '45:14 §', '45:21-22', '46:5' (contains non-ASCII § and ranges).
Song values have leading/trailing spaces (' The Way', ' Everybody Have Fun Tonight ').
Weeks_on_Top is REAL but stores whole numbers (3.0,1.0,2.0), only 3 distinct.
Date_of_ceremony has distinct=1 (single value '18 February 2011') -> Date/String range degenerate.
Tiny tables (7/10/9 rows); FK volume.Artist_ID has 5 distinct of 7 parents (not all artists referenced); music_festival.Volume 9 distinct of 10.
FK chain artist <- volume <- music_festival; both FKs point to single-column INT PKs (unique parents, no dangling).
PKs are INT single-column; no composite keys, no self-references.
operator_ts_expectations: Artist_ID/Volume_ID/ID/Age/Volume/Weeks_on_Top -> Number fuzzer: uniform ints/floats in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-1/+-2 perturbation; Age will get implausible values (negatives, huge).
Weeks_on_Top REAL -> Number scale from 'real' (no args) -> wide float range, not the 1-3 observed.

Artist, Famous_Title, Volume_Issue, Issue_Date, Song, Music_Festival, Category, Result, Date_of_ceremony -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20 plus contamination, so date-like text becomes gibberish -> FN on date-format predicates.
Date_of_ceremony single distinct value: String sampler range [len,len+1] narrow but still random chars; loses the '18 February 2011' shape.

FK columns drawn from parent's final values with replacement -> duplicates in child FK, and only 5-7 distinct parent keys -> many-to-one ties created (good for joins, may create FP on DISTINCT/count queries).
PK dedup keeps first occurrence; with tiny sizes (level0=1+30u, x4) tables may be small or empty -> empty-result FPs.
String contamination (prefix/suffix/drop char) breaks equality/join on text columns -> FN on exact-match predicates.
Number perturbation on Artist_ID/Volume_ID may break FK consistency only if drawn fresh; FK path uses parent values so joins survive, but non-FK numeric predicates get implausible values.
Date text columns never get the Date fuzzer, so TS cannot produce 'November 2007'-style values -> misses on LIKE '%2007%' or month-name predicates.
Leading/trailing spaces in Song are not preserved by String fuzzer -> FN on TRIM/equality queries.
Tiny original sizes mean TS's 30-200 row sizes are much larger than original -> cardinality-based FPs (e.g. count comparisons).
